title: Nieuwland et al. 2018: Multi-site N400 Replication Study
description: A large-scale (N=356) multi-laboratory EEG replication of DeLong, Urbach & Kutas (2005), testing whether readers pre-activate the phonological form of upcoming nouns during sentence comprehension. Participants at nine UK laboratories read sentences word-by-word in which the indefinite articles a/an preceded highly expected or unexpected nouns. Reliable N400 effects were found on target nouns but not on the preceding articles, which challenges strong accounts of probabilistic prediction. Events are enriched with stimulus metadata such as cloze probability and plausibility.
methods_description: EEG was recorded at nine UK laboratories using BioSemi BDF, BrainVision and Neuroscan CNT systems (32 to 128 channels, 250 to 2048 Hz). Participants read sentences by RSVP (200 ms word, 300 ms blank) with 80 DeLong replication sentences and 80 control sentences, using two counterbalanced stimulus lists. Comprehension questions were asked on a subset of trials. The raw data are unfiltered and unresampled. The study followed a pre-registered protocol.
